description: Machine-readable validation spec for the MCP chatbox. Defines type, default, limits, and warnings for every numerical parameter in the config pipeline. Source-verified against Julia code and corrected by domain expert experience.

validation_levels.error: Reject input — will crash or produce nonsense
validation_levels.warning: Allow but flag — may be inefficient or inaccurate
validation_levels.info: Informational hint — user may want to reconsider

S.description: Spin quantum number per site. Local Hilbert space dimension d = 2S+1.
S.constraint: Must satisfy: 2S+1 is a positive integer (i.e., S = 0.5, 1.0, 1.5, 2.0, 2.5, ...)

validation.message: High spin values are uncommon. Most quantum spin chain studies use S ≤ 2.

N.description: Number of spin sites in the chain.

validation.message: N must be at least 2.
Tensor network algorithms require N ≥ 3 due to MPO structure.

validation.check: N > ed_limit and algorithm in [ed_spectrum, ed_time_evolution]
validation.message: System too large for exact diagonalization. Use DMRG or TDVP instead.

0.5.note: N=14 requires ~4 GB RAM for dense diagonalization. N ≤ 12 recommended.

1.0.note: d=3, Hilbert space D=3^N grows fast. N=10 requires ~30 GB RAM.

N_spins.description: Number of spin sites in spinboson system (boson site is separate). Total sites = N_spins + 1.

validation.message: Need at least 1 spin site.
Hilbert space too large for ED. Reduce N_spins or nmax.

N_spins.ed_guidance: With nmax=4, S=0.5: N_spins=8 (D=1280, trivial), N_spins=10 (D=5120, ~200 MB), N_spins=12 (D=20480, ~3 GB, near limit).

nmax.description: Maximum boson occupation number (Fock space cutoff). Boson Hilbert space dimension = nmax+1.

validation.message: nmax must be at least 1. A single Fock state (nmax=0) has no dynamics.
nmax > 16 is rarely needed. Check that higher Fock states are populated before increasing.

dtype.description: Numerical data type for tensors and operators.

validation.message: dtype must be 'ComplexF64' or 'Float64'.

validation.check: dtype == 'Float64' and model uses Y, Sp, or Sm operators
validation.message: Float64 is incompatible with complex operators (Y, Sp, Sm). Use ComplexF64.

rules.Float64: Safe only when ALL operators are real: X, Z, I (spin) and a, adag, Bn, Ib (boson).
rules.ComplexF64: Always safe. Required when any operator is Y, Sp, or Sm. Use when in doubt.

krylov_dim.description: Krylov subspace dimension for the Lanczos eigensolver. Controls the local eigenvalue solve at each bond.

validation.message: krylov_dim must be at least 1.
From extensive testing, krylov_dim=4 is optimal for global DMRG convergence. Larger or smaller values can impair convergence.
Very large krylov_dim is costly per local solve and rarely improves global convergence.

max_iter.description: Maximum Lanczos restart iterations per local site solve.

validation.message: max_iter must be at least 1.
max_iter < 8 may not achieve local convergence. Recommended minimum is 8.
max_iter > 20 is usually unnecessary. The sweet spot for serious convergence is around 14.

chi_max.description: Maximum MPS bond dimension. Controls how much entanglement the MPS can represent. DMRG truncates SVD to this dimension after each two-site update.

validation.message: chi_max must be at least 1.

notes.complexity: Time complexity scales as O(chi³ · d² · N) per sweep. Memory scales as O(chi² · d · N). Doubling chi_max increases runtime ~8x.
notes.exact_recovery: When chi = d^(N/2) (e.g. 2^(N/2) for spin-1/2), the MPS representation is exact and recovers the full Hilbert space.
notes.entanglement: Highly entangled systems (e.g. critical systems, systems near quantum phase transitions) require larger chi_max for accurate results. Gapped systems converge with moderate chi_max.
notes.convergence_workflow: Start at chi_max=64. Converge by doubling: 64 → 128 → 256. Converged when observables stop changing.

cutoff.description: SVD truncation cutoff. Singular values below this threshold (after normalization) are discarded. Acts alongside chi_max — whichever is more restrictive wins.

validation.message: cutoff must be positive.
cutoff must be less than 1 (singular values are normalized).
Very small cutoff is expensive and rarely needed. 1e-10 is the practical lower limit.
Large cutoff aggressively truncates the MPS. Results may lose accuracy.

local_dim.description: Local Hilbert space dimension per site. AUTO-DERIVED from system S: d = floor(2*S + 1). Never set manually.

n_sweeps.description: Total number of DMRG sweeps. Each sweep is one full left-right-left pass over all bonds.

validation.message: n_sweeps must be at least 1.
Most systems converge within 100 sweeps. If energy is still changing after 200 sweeps, consider increasing chi_max instead.

notes.convergence: Monitor |E(n) - E(n-1)| between sweeps. Converged when this drops below ~1e-8. Critical systems or systems with a small spectral gap may need significantly more sweeps and may not converge within the default range. If convergence is slow, increase n_sweeps rather than giving up.

krylov_dim.description: Krylov subspace dimension for the matrix exponential solver. Controls the number of local Krylov iterations per time step.

validation.message: krylov_dim must be at least 1.
krylov_dim < 10 may not converge the local time step. Recommended minimum is 10.
krylov_dim > 20 is costly per time step. The sweet spot is around 14.

tol.description: Convergence tolerance for the Krylov exponential. The solver checks element-wise convergence and stops when all components are within tol.

validation.message: tol must be positive.
tol < 1e-10 is very tight and expensive. May require larger krylov_dim. 1e-10 is the practical lower limit.
tol > 1e-6 may produce inaccurate local time steps.
evol_type must be 'real' or 'imaginary'. This is enforced by a hard assertion in the code.

value_descriptions.real: Real time evolution: e^{-iHdt}. Unitary, norm-preserving. Use for quantum dynamics, quench problems, time-dependent observables.
value_descriptions.imaginary: Imaginary time evolution: e^{-Hdt}. Non-unitary, converges toward ground state. Alternative to DMRG for ground state search in hard convergence cases.

dt.description: Time step per sweep. Each sweep advances the state by dt. Total simulated time = dt × n_sweeps.

validation.message: dt must be positive.
Extremely small dt means many more sweeps to reach a given total time, which accumulates truncation error.
Large dt increases Trotter-like error per step. Consider reducing dt and increasing n_sweeps.

notes.error_tradeoff: TDVP has two competing error sources. (1) Trotter error: O(dt²) per sweep from the two-site splitting — shrinks with smaller dt. (2) Truncation error: accumulated per sweep from SVD truncation at chi_max — does not depend on dt directly, but more sweeps (needed when dt is small to reach the same total time) means more accumulated truncation error. There is a sweet spot: very small dt reduces Trotter error but increases total truncation error. Very large dt reduces the number of sweeps but increases Trotter error per step. A good starting point is dt=0.05.

chi_max.description: Maximum MPS bond dimension during time evolution. Entanglement grows under generic dynamics, so chi_max must capture the entanglement at the final time.

validation.message: chi_max must be at least 1.

notes.complexity: Time complexity scales as O(chi³ · d² · N) per sweep. Memory scales as O(chi² · d · N). Doubling chi_max increases runtime ~8x.
notes.exact_recovery: When chi = d^(N/2) (e.g. 2^(N/2) for spin-1/2), the MPS is exact and recovers the full Hilbert space.
notes.entanglement_growth: Under generic (non-integrable) dynamics, entanglement grows linearly in time. chi_max must be large enough for the final simulation time. For long-time simulations, chi_max=256 or higher may be needed.

cutoff.description: SVD truncation cutoff for MPS compression after each time step. Works alongside chi_max.

validation.message: cutoff must be positive.
cutoff must be less than 1.
Very small cutoff is expensive and rarely needed.
Large cutoff aggressively truncates. Results may lose accuracy.

n_sweeps.description: Total number of time steps (sweeps). Total simulated time = dt × n_sweeps. This is the user's choice based on the desired total simulation time.

validation.message: n_sweeps must be at least 1.

ed_spectrum.system_requirements: N must be within ED limits (see system.N.ed_limits_by_S)

n_states.description: Number of lowest eigenstates to compute. If null or omitted, computes the full spectrum (all D eigenstates).

validation.message: n_states must be at least 1.

validation.check: n_states is set and n_states > D
validation.message: n_states cannot exceed Hilbert space dimension D. Code will crash with assertion error.

use_sparse.description: Whether to use sparse (Lanczos-based) diagonalization instead of dense LAPACK.

validation.check: use_sparse == true and n_states is null
validation.message: use_sparse=true without n_states will be ignored — full spectrum always uses dense diagonalization. You will lose access to the full spectrum. Set n_states if you only need a few lowest states.

notes.dense: Dense diagonalization (use_sparse=false): Computes all D eigenstates via LAPACK. Reliable. Required for full spectrum.
notes.sparse: Sparse diagonalization (use_sparse=true): Uses Arpack Lanczos for only the lowest n_states. Faster for large D with small n_states. Only used when n_states is set AND n_states < D/2 AND D > 20.

ed_time_evolution.system_requirements: N must be within ED limits (see system.N.ed_limits_by_S)

dt.description: Time step between saved snapshots. The state is evolved exactly using eigendecomposition — dt controls only output resolution, NOT accuracy.

validation.message: dt must be positive.

notes.accuracy: Unlike TDVP, ED time evolution is numerically exact (machine precision). dt has zero effect on accuracy — it only determines how often snapshots are saved. Choose dt based on desired time resolution of observables.

n_steps.description: Number of time steps to simulate. Total simulated time = dt × n_steps. User's choice based on desired total simulation time.

validation.message: n_steps must be at least 1.

cross_parameter_constraints.message: DMRG and TDVP require at least 3 sites due to MPO structure.

cross_parameter_constraints.description: ED algorithms have hard system size limits
cross_parameter_constraints.message: System too large for exact diagonalization. Hilbert space dimension D = d^N exceeds practical memory limits. Consider DMRG (ground state) or TDVP (time evolution) instead.

cross_parameter_constraints.condition: dtype == 'Float64' and any operator in model is Y, Sp, or Sm
cross_parameter_constraints.message: The model uses complex operators (Y, S+, or S-). dtype must be ComplexF64.

cross_parameter_constraints.description: Sparse diagonalization without n_states is pointless
cross_parameter_constraints.condition: algorithm == 'ed_spectrum' and use_sparse == true and n_states is null
cross_parameter_constraints.message: use_sparse=true is ignored for full spectrum — dense diagonalization is always used. Set n_states to use sparse solver, but note you will lose the full spectrum.
local_dim is automatically computed from S (d = 2S+1). Your value will be overwritten.

cross_parameter_constraints.description: ED time evolution requires an initial state
cross_parameter_constraints.condition: algorithm == 'ed_time_evolution' and state is not provided
cross_parameter_constraints.message: ED time evolution requires an initial state to evolve. Provide a state configuration.

cross_parameter_constraints.description: TN algorithms require an initial state
cross_parameter_constraints.condition: algorithm in ['dmrg', 'tdvp'] and state is not provided
cross_parameter_constraints.message: DMRG and TDVP require an initial MPS state. Provide a state configuration.
